title: NO KINGS Woodstock
description:
Trump wants a military parade. We’re giving him a history lesson.

On June 14, while Trump spends millions of taxpayer dollars celebrating his own birthday with tanks and pageantry, Indivisible Woodstock CAN will join communities across the country for No Kings—a national day of action against authoritarianism and billionaire corruption.

Flag Day isn’t about glorifying a man. It marks the birth of the U.S. Army—the day our nation first stood up to a king. Now Trump wants to twist that legacy into a monument to himself. We’re here to say: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

✊ WHY WE’RE MOBILIZING
This isn’t just political disagreement. It’s a coordinated power grab.

He’s using our tax dollars to throw his party—while they slash Social Security and gut Medicaid.

He’s defied courts, disappeared people, and threatened dissenters.

He’s pushing for a third term and building a machine to rule, not govern.

We’re done being quiet. We’re done pretending this is normal.
This is our country, and we’re showing up to defend it.

🎖️ WHO THIS IS FOR
Whether you’re a veteran who took the oath…
A parent worried about your child’s future…
Or a neighbor who just knows this isn’t right…

This moment is for you.
Come stand with us in visible, nonviolent resistance. Let’s show the country what real patriotism looks like.

🔔 WHAT TO EXPECT
Peaceful rally and sidewalk demonstration—we’ll stay on sidewalks and paved areas and will not block traffic or pedestrians.

Speakers including veterans and community members

A first aid/shade tent nearby

Signs, chants, flags, and a united front against corruption

🧭 WHAT TO BRING & WEAR
Wear red, white, and blue

If you’ve served or are currently serving, feel free to wear military attire

Bring water, sunscreen, and a sign if you’ve got one

🛡️ OUR COMMUNITY GUIDELINES
Stay peaceful and nonviolent

Do not bring weapons (even legally permitted ones)

Do not engage with agitators or counter-protesters

Follow the lead of our trained volunteers and coordinators

Keep public areas accessible and safe for all

This is a nationwide mobilization to reject strongman rule and stand up for the people. We’re not spectators. We’re the story.

On June 14, while Trump spends millions of taxpayer dollars celebrating his own birthday with tanks and pageantry, Indivisible Woodstock CAN will join communities across the country for No Kings—a national day of action against authoritarianism and billionaire corruption.

Flag Day isn’t about glorifying a man. It marks the birth of the U.S. Army—the day our nation first stood up to a king. Now Trump wants to twist that legacy into a monument to himself. We’re here to say: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

✊ WHY WE’RE MOBILIZING
This isn’t just political disagreement. It’s a coordinated power grab.

He’s using our tax dollars to throw his party—while they slash Social Security and gut Medicaid.

He’s defied courts, disappeared people, and threatened dissenters.

He’s pushing for a third term and building a machine to rule, not govern.

We’re done being quiet. We’re done pretending this is normal.
This is our country, and we’re showing up to defend it.

🎖️ WHO THIS IS FOR
Whether you’re a veteran who took the oath…
A parent worried about your child’s future…
Or a neighbor who just knows this isn’t right…

This moment is for you.
Come stand with us in visible, nonviolent resistance. Let’s show the country what real patriotism looks like.

🔔 WHAT TO EXPECT
Peaceful rally and sidewalk demonstration—we’ll stay on sidewalks and paved areas and will not block traffic or pedestrians.

Speakers including veterans and community members

A first aid/shade tent nearby

Signs, chants, flags, and a united front against corruption

🧭 WHAT TO BRING & WEAR
Wear red, white, and blue

If you’ve served or are currently serving, feel free to wear military attire

Bring water, sunscreen, and a sign if you’ve got one

🛡️ OUR COMMUNITY GUIDELINES
Stay peaceful and nonviolent

Do not bring weapons (even legally permitted ones)

Do not engage with agitators or counter-protesters

Follow the lead of our trained volunteers and coordinators

Keep public areas accessible and safe for all

This is a nationwide mobilization to reject strongman rule and stand up for the people. We’re not spectators. We’re the story.

HOSTED BY:
Indivisible Woodstock CAN
📧 woodstockcan@proton.me
📣 Instagram: @indivisiblewoodstockcan
🌐 www.woodstockcan.com

location.venue: South Coast Air Quality Management District Headquarters

description:
Everyone deserves clean, safe air at home. But SoCal families are stuck breathing some of the dirtiest air in the country, causing asthma, illness, and even early death.

This doesn't have to be our reality. We can ditch the dangerous gas appliances and switch to safer electric alternatives. 

Our local air regulators are voting on rules that could finally increase our choices for healthier, gas-free homes.

The gas industry is pushing back and fighting to keep electric options off store shelves. Why? Profit over people. 

Let's make sure they hear us, not gas industry lobbying. Join us on June 6th to demand clean air and healthy homes!

📅 Join us to rally for clean air on Friday, June 6 at 8 a.m.

After the rally, you can comment at the 9 a.m. SCAQMD board meeting to tell the board: Pass strong rules, no more delays, no more weakening and why you care.

title: NO KINGS ROANOKE
description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**
NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.

🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨

And not just any movement - in Roanoke we’re inviting you to come together to build community, in joyful, musical, art and family-filled rebellion, standing in solidarity to demand a government and economy that ensures access to opportunity and a better life for all of us.

## What to bring

Bring picnic blankets, instruments, art (think Daisy Art Parade big!), bubble machines, family, pets, etc. There will be live music, performance artists, and more. This is about coming together as a community, showing our numbers, and building the strength of our movement through deeper connection to one another.

## Location
2020 Andrews Rd NW, Roanoke, VA 24017

## Schedule
* 10am - 11:30am - listen to the band, talk with one another, engage with organizers and crowd marshals to learn more about what you can do to build this movement.

* 11:30am - 12pm - join the Juneteenth Family Reunion walk (https://maps.app.goo.gl/5oJ8X2cBGN1bzDeT7) across McCadden park to 1122 19th St NW, Roanoke. Please respect organizers and the event theme of freedom and unity and leave behind any protest signs you’ve brought before you begin the walk.

* 12pm - stay as long as you like and enjoy the festivities at the (Juneteenth Family Reunion!)(https://www.facebook.com/events/889600673307347/) Keep meeting and talking to folks and finding new ways to plug into your community.

## Support
* Support Juneteenth organizers by donating towards activities and food (water & hotdogs) for kids at the event via (Roanoke Cultural Collective)(https://linktr.ee/roanokeculturalcollective) 

* Send via CashApp ($RCC1865) or check, payable to Roanoke Cultural Collective, P.O. Box 12412, Roanoke, VA 24025

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: South Suburban Relentless Protect Our Rights
description: You are an amazing group! All heroes in our eyes! We have news about TWO events! Yes TWO! So read carefully! The site and time will be the same, the dates will be different. So on Saturday May 31st we will gather at 147th and the East side of LaGrange Road in Orland Park at 11am until 1pm. This is a peaceful protest. Please do not engage with any counter protesters.  Some do not like this approach but we have found it to be the most successful way of having our voices heard and enjoying the community we have developed. There will be monitors on site if a de-escalation is needed.  On Saturday the 14th of June we will gather at the above mentioned place and same time for NO KINGS DAY. We know there are bigger venues but feel that some of our  most vulnerable that cannot make those trips have the same opportunity as everyone. We get people from nearby and far away! We post on many platforms so we do draw a great mix of people! On some platforms we are South Suburban Relentless and also Protect Our Rights.  Our last protest had a head count of over 100 and I heard one of our group say there were 150 supporters of OUR RGHTS that attended! Ten, Fifty or Hundreds, we are all fighting the good fight and on the right side of history.  As always bring a chair if you need a break. Bring water and friends! See you there! When injustice becomes law, resistance becomes duty! Kathy and Sharon.
accessibility_notes: Park in the mall parking lot. There is a small embankment.

- Our Freedom of Speech and other liberties under the Constitution

- Our colleges, universities, teachers and students

- Our LGBTQIA+ siblings

- Our immigrant friends and neighbors

- Our national parks and public lands

- Our food, water and air safety

- Our reproductive rights and our freedom to vote

- Our democracy!

description:

Every Thursday, @ 7 am, we'll gather on the north east corner of Central and Monte Vista, right in front of the ICE Field office.

description:

title: NO KINGS: A Marin-wide Mobilization: Novato City Hall
description:
## Time to Rain on This Wannabe King’s Parade
June 14 is Flag Day and Trump’s birthday—and he’s throwing himself a $45 million military-style birthday bash. With our tax dollars. We say: NO KINGS. YES TO THE PEOPLE.

Join in this **county-wide #NoKings takeover** with 20+ pop-up protests all across Marin. One loud, visible, united stand against Trump’s grift and power grab.

➡️ Check the protest locations and pick yours: [mobilize.us/nokings](https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/?country=US&per_page=25&q=Marin-wide)

## 🪧 What to Bring:
Make your own protest sign:
- Cut a **heart-shaped sign** from poster board (a good size is around 18x24" or larger)
- Write: **“NO KINGS, YES _______”** (Fill in the blank with what you believe in— like democracy, healthcare, education, social security, the law, the people, etc.)

Get bold and creative. This country needs more love for people—not billionaires.

👑 Marin doesn’t kneel.

💖 We rise together.

Bring friends. Show up big on **June 14**. 

Sponsored by Indivisible Novato.

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. All participants agree to assume 100% responsibility for their own safety, conduct and well-being._
accessibility_notes: This event involves protesting with your homemade signs in front of City Hall and nearby sidewalks.

title: Freedom Fridays: We Stand By Ukraine
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

Slava Ukraini!!! We must never forget the nightmare the Ukrainian people are still living. Join us at noon with your signs and Ukrainian flags on May 30th at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue, Williamsburg. Together, we will show our support for this brave nation who fights for DEMOCRACY every moment.

It will be hot so please, do not forget a cold beverage and dress appropriately for the weather - maybe a hat or umbrella.

COMMUNITY NORMS
Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”. 
Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS!
If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts and an Indivisible Cap or Tricorn Hat. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

title: Scarsdale, NY: Stop the Con Ed Rate Hikes!
description:
Our bills are too high! That's why residents of Scarsdale and neighboring municipalities will be joining together on May 30th at the Scarsdale library, energy bills in hand, calling on the state legislature to pass the NY HEAT Act now!

The NY HEAT Act is critical legislation currently being discussed in Albany that will lower our Con Ed gas bills.

With costs going up on groceries and other expenses due to federal tariffs, we need our state government to step up and offer solutions that will offset the federal government’s irresponsible and dangerous economic decisions.

We'll be joining with state legislators including Assemblymember Amy Paulin and Senator Shelley Mayer who are representing us by working to pass the NY HEAT Act this legislative session!  

Cosponsored by Indivisible Scarsdale, NYCD16/15 Indivisible, Mothers Out Front, Westchester for Change and United for Clean Energy.

description:
Join other Houstonians in protesting outside John Cornyn’s Houston office (on Memorial Drive) to raise awareness of your objection to recent government actions.

The Cornyn Houston Office Protest has been on Houston streets each Tuesday for over 8 years. Fully independent, the Cornyn Protest has been sustained by a dedicated core of Houstonians. The protest sets the example of people showing up for themselves no matter what.

title: Protest to Support our LGBTQ+ Community
description:
This a local Indivisible event!
Protest to Support our LGBTQ+ Community

Date: Sunday, June 22nd 
Time: 4:00PM-5:30PM
Location: Hyannis Airport Rotary (details about parking and where exactly to stand listed below.) 
Please wear “pride spirit” to make a visual impact as a rainbow sea of love, acceptance, and appreciation for diversity and all the unique talents that makes our community so vibrant. 
As always, please bring signs, flags, drums, other instruments, chants, art, etc., as joy is resistance, art is resistance, community is resistance. [Joyful community resistance to fascism]

In honor/celebration of pride month, we are protesting against Trump & his administration, specifically against the harm he has caused to the LGBTQ+ community. We are infuriated with his executive orders that ban gender affirming care for minors, that restrict trans rights, and that eliminate protections against discrimination for those in the LGBTQ+ community. We recognize the detrimental effect this has had on the well being of many individuals and the community as a whole. We stand in solidarity to say we will not put up with this.
We will not allow this administration’s attacks on the LGBTQ+ community to continue! #RESIST
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

******Corruption destroys, Community Builds: We will also be collecting nonperishable food items for the AIDS support group in Hyannis. ******

We are being cosponsored by a local pride group, and have invited local pride groups to set up informational tables if they are available. 

As with every protest, we also want to highlight the extreme unconstitutional practices of this administration, as this is not just about policies. 
This is NOT business as usual in DC, this is NOT normal. 

This republican administration has attempted to seize control over state election processes through executive orders and efforts to undermine civil rights legislation, as well as threatening the checks and balances established by the Constitution, such as disregarding court orders and altering federal regulations without proper authority.​​ The administration is using its current power to help billionaires continue to profit while striping away the services that help the most needy. 

We need to stand up for due process, free speech, upholding court rulings, and the separation of church and state. The Founding Fathers established the principles of due process, free speech, and the separation of church and state through the First Amendment and other parts of the Constitution. These concepts were designed to protect individual rights and limit government power. 
We have NO KINGS in America, yet Trump is acting like one. 
We, the people, must rise up, and show that the power of the people is greater than the people in power. 

Protest Homework (aka, protest action steps)
5 Calls App or Website, National Action Steps:
Scroll down to the LGBTQ+ section, as of right now there are 2 calls to make (to all 3 of your members of congress!):
1. *“condemn RFK Jr’s False Report on Transgender Youth Treatment” and 
2. *“Oppose Efforts to Dehumanize transgender and LGBTQ+ people” 
If you have time for another round of calls, please scroll to “executive overreach” and click:
3. *”fight the trump administration’s defiance of the constitution and courts”

title: Freedom Fridays: Let's Celebrate Pride Month
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL,  RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

The last few years in America have seen a record number of bills that attack LGBTQIA+ rights, and now the attack from Trump is targeting transgender military members.
According to USA Today, "The Supreme Court has ruled against transgender people serving in the military, legitimizing President Donald Trump's discriminatory agenda.
On May 6, the nation's highest court decided to allow Trump’s trans military ban to take effect after a lower court had halted its enforcement. Because the decision was part of the “shadow docket” ‒ emergency appeals decided without full briefing or oral argument, and without any written opinion ‒ we don’t know why the justices ruled this way or how the vote was divided, although the three liberal judges on the court say they would have rejected the request that the case be heard." https://www.usatoday.com/.../supreme-court.../83499410007/ .

address_lines: Intersection of Silver St. and Leyden Rd, Greenfield, MA

description:
Stand up for democracy with Franklin County neighbors and people up and down the Valley! Hundreds of us will stand with banners and signs on seven I-91 overpasses in Franklin County at the same time that people stand out on I-91 overpasses from Connecticut up to Vermont. We’ll be visible to thousands of people driving on I-91 during the Friday evening commute and the beginning of Memorial Day weekend.

Franklin County’s I-91 overpass standouts are being organized by Franklin County Continuing the Political Revolution (FCCPR), Indivisible West Quabbin and Gill Indivisible. We The People stand to raise awareness about attacks on our society by the Trump administration.

We The People stand to:

•Save the Constitution •Save Medicare •Save Medicaid •Save Social Security •Save Veteran’s Services •Save funding to universities and non-profits •Save the Department of Education •Save EPA •Save NOAA •Save libraries •Save Head Start •Stop ICE from kidnapping people •Stop attacks on free speech •Stop the othering of the queer/transgender community

We stand to RESIST!

Bring signs and banners with LARGE BOLD messages so they can be read by drivers on I-91.

This action is legal and nonviolent. Safety is essential… take care with parking and walking to/from the overpass and during the standout.  Parking is available on Place Terrace St. and the Academy of Early Learning on Place Terrace.  If more parking is needed, please park at the bottom of Nash's Mill Rd.

Accessibility
Notes from the organizer: This event is NOT wheelchair accessible and requires walking to/from the overpass and stepping up/down onto a sidewalk.

Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information.

title: NO KINGS Milpitas
description:
Wannabe king/dictator Donald Trump is throwing himself a birthday celebration that’s expected to cost tens of millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.  That same day, we will rally to oppose his corruption, illegal activities, and violation of the basis of our democracy – the U. S. Constitution – to which all veterans swear an oath to uphold.

### The Milpitas rally will be Saturday, June 14 from 10:00 AM till noon in front of City Hall. 

## Sign Up to join us and get updates!

This country doesn’t belong to a king—and we’re not letting a wannabe king throw himself a taxpayer-funded parade while slashing both our civil rights and the programs our families and communities depend on. No Kings is a nationwide day of defiance to reject authoritarianism—and show the world what democracy really looks like.

The Army’s birthday isn’t about parades or pageantry — it marks the beginning of America’s rejection of kings.  On June 14, 1775, the Continental Congress created the U.S. Army to oppose a monarch who claimed absolute power. Now, 250 years later, Donald Trump wants to twist that legacy into a personal celebration of himself – yet another example of him corrupting our government.

On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings. Using the principles of nonviolence and peaceful protest, we will stand together to oppose any king wannabe.

**No Kings Day in cities across the country!**  See the map: [https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/map/](https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/map/)

### No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

In Milpitas, we are standing for democracy, the U. S. Constitution, and the rule of law. 

Even if you cannot attend, use your social media and email lists to spread the word. Find graphics [here](https://brandfolder.com/s/vqbb79z4p6hhkgkrxwp9nh). 

Remember to bring noise-makers: drums, cowbells, whistles, and empty soda cans filled with beans/pebbles!

**50501 is a peaceful movement.  Violence of any kind will not be tolerated.**

title: May 31- Stand Up for Democracy - Seminole County Protest

location.venue: Parking lots along 17-92 near Casselberry City Hall (across from Target)

description:
Trump has gone too far. He is abusing authority and undermining the foundations of our democracy.

Stand up for democracy with us! Join our peaceful demonstration on Saturday, May 31, from 10 am to noon along South 17-92 in Casselberry.

We will gather along South Highway 17-92 between East Melody Lane and Triplet Lake Dr. (This is near the Casselberry Target but on the OTHER SIDE of the street, close to Casselberry City Hall.) There is parking close to the sidewalks. 

Our focus is on being visible to passing cars and showing that we love America. We encourage people to wear red, white and blue, and bring flags to wave. 

We encourage you to bring a chair, umbrella (for shade or rain), water, and snacks. Wear comfortable shoes and clothing.

If you aren't able to stand by the road with us, then drive by and honk! 

Bring your favorite sign with a message that is meaningful to you. Or you can borrow one of our signs to hold while you are there. 

To make a sign, buy foam board at Dollar Tree or other discount stores. Be sure to decorate both sides. Thick markers work well.

You can also sign up for a SemDems sign-making event, or come to the SemDems office during office hours to use supplies to make a sign there. 

Weather Advisory: If there is excessive rain and lightning, or the weather is not safe for you, please prioritize your safety and join us at a different protest.

**Please note** A core principle behind our actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

This event will also be posted on the fiftyfifty.one website.

title: No Kings Day Citizens' Parade in Wilmington
description:
Hosted by Indivisible Highlands and Beyond; co-hosted with 302 United and Delaware Working Families Power.

Come out for Wilmington’s "No Kings Citizens' Parade" as part of the June 14th National Day of Defiance to counter Trump's ridiculous $45 million birthday parade in DC on this same day. Join us as we parade down Wilmington's own Pennsylvania Avenue to say "NO KINGS!"

June 14th is Flag Day and also the 250th birthday of the army — a day that marks when Americans first organized to stand up to a king. "Trump isn’t honoring that legacy. He’s hijacking it to celebrate himself."

“This country doesn’t belong to a king — and we’re not letting him throw himself a parade funded by tens of millions of our taxpayer dollars while stealing from us and stripping away our rights, our freedoms, and the programs our families rely on. On June 14th, we’re coming together to send one clear message: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.”

We will gather at the corner of Pennsylvania Avenue and N. Bancroft Parkway in Wilmington. Specifically, we'll meet on grass lawn between the two sides of N. Bancroft Parkway - on the Wawaset Park side of PA Ave., between PA Ave. and W. 11th St. - and march/walk on the sidewalk along Pennsylvania Avenue toward Tower Hill School. 

A short pre-parade rally (with music and guest speakers) will precede the parade. The full roundtrip march is 1.3 miles long.

Bring flags and signs (two-sided, if possible) as well as kazoos, drums, cowbells, etc.

If walking isn't possible for you, please come anyway - with signs and flags - and be part of a Honk and Wave rally along Pennsylvania Ave. 

Parking is available on N. Bancroft Parkway and surrounding streets. 

Given our commitment to nonviolent action, we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. If you encounter a heckler or counter-protester (organized or unorganized, from a simple raised finger to a verbal taunt), the rule of thumb is to IGNORE IT!! Do not engage. If necessary, simply turn your back - or walk away.

This event is a great opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals who are passionate about making a positive impact on our community. **Mutual aid drive: Entire duration of event**

The United States has never hosted a major military parade that wasn't either during wartime or to mark the end of a war. On June 14, Trump plans to host a military parade on the 250th anniversary of the Army's founding, as well as his birthday. This is his second attempt to plan one, after a failed attempt for Veterans Day of 2018.

If Trump wants a birthday party, let's give him one to remember.

Come join us at the Michigan State Capitol Building as we stand up for democracy and oppose the Trump Administration's attacks on the rights and livelihoods of Michiganders, Americans, and vulnerable people around the world. We will protest, hear fiery speeches, have 1-on-1 conversations with politicians, march in solidarity with a parade in front, and throw a carnival to highlight the absurdity of the military parade Trump has planned on his birthday.

We are planning to have food trucks, games, street performers, and other activities in the theme of a carnival. Feel free to dress as creatively as you like.

We are also planning to host a mutual aid drive throughout the event, accepting shelf-stable foods, hygiene supplies, sexual health supplies, gender-affirming items, first aid supplies, and gently used clothing.

Be sure to invite your friends!

**Want to learn more about 50501MI? Visit our website at https://50501michigan.com**

accessibility_notes:
Visitors requiring an accessible entrance to the Roundhouse/State Capitol can be dropped off near the accessible ramp in the visitor parking lot on the east side of the building or use accessible parking in that lot.

The entrance to the visitor parking lot is off Paseo de Peralta, just before the intersection of Paseo de Peralta and Old Santa Fe Trail (directly across the street from Kaune's/the two-way street). There is a drop off section where people hold their signs. There should be a ramp there. If you want to get as close as possible, there is an option to turn left on the side of Roundhouse/State Capitol and you can pull up to the curb at the crosswalk where a ramp is located.

There is also an accessible entrance to the Roundhouse/State Capitol through "Capitol North" on Don Gaspar Avenue (the one-way street). Follow the blue accessibility signs to the ramp and to the accessible entrance. This option will not accommodate someone with limited mobility who needs direct access and requires a shorter distance.

Physical Address: 490 Old Santa Fe Trail, Santa Fe, NM 87501
Free parking is available Monday through Friday at 420 Galisteo St.

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE Field Office in Phoenix
description:
Big events with thousands of people are great. But we also need local, more frequent rallies that show locals that they're not alone in this fight.

**When we realized the DHS/ICE field office is in our neighborhood, we decided it would be the perfect place for an ICE-specific RhRR!**

Every Thursday @ 7:00 am, we'll gather on the south east corner of Central and Monte Vista, right in front of the ICE Field office.

**STAY ON THE SIDEWALK!** It's public property and we've a right to be there. Be sure you **DO NOT BLOCK** access to the building—that means cars as well as people.

**Please make ICE-specific signs**, as we're here to show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone and the ICE staffers that We The People care about due process for everyone.

Spread the word. Come join us. All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us/#museum-district).

Love this idea and want to start your own Rush-hour Resistance Rally in your area? Groovy! [Let's make that happen!](https://rhrr.us/#start-your-own)

title: Hands Off Our Veterans / Veterans Against Fascism

address_lines: Paseo Del Pueblo Norte & Civic Plaza Drive

description:
Join us on Friday, June 6 from 12:00 to 1:00 at the corner of Paseo del Pueblo Norte and Civic Plaza Drive for a peaceful protest. Bring your protest signs and a folding chair if you can’t stand for an hour or so. Please stay on the sidewalks, don't step into the street and only cross at designated crosswalks.

A massive rally is planned in Washington, D.C., and elsewhere on June 6, the 81st anniversary of D-Day, to protest cuts at the Department of Veteran Affairs and call for the protection of veterans' benefits and jobs, which are being slashed by the Trump administration's efforts. Nearly 30% of the federal workforce is made up of veterans, the proposed job cuts will disproportionately affect that population.

Veterans, family members and anyone who supports the service and sacrifice of the armed forces are encouraged to join us in support of former service members who work for the federal government and for the preservation of VA benefits.

Rallies are a great way to meet other like-minded community members. They remind us that we aren’t alone and it feels good to be civically engaged. Action is the antidote to despair. We guarantee you will feel better about the state of affairs when you leave this event.

Please follow all posted rules and traffic laws when attending a rally. Safety is always our first priority. Please stay on the sidewalks, don't step into the street and only cross at designated crosswalks.

title: No Kings: Let Freedom Fly - Brattleboro Indivisible
description:
No Kings! Let Freedom Fly in downtown Brattleboro on Flag Day! 

On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets again nationwide, standing together in love and unity. Our movement is building - to support justice, a sane society, a stronger world. We stand declaring that the power belongs with the people. That’s US! That’s each and every one of YOU! 

Come out and make some noise with us in Brattleboro! We’ll gather at Centre Congregational Church at 3:00 pm, parade with The People's Resistance Marching Band and Becky Graber’s street choir to end up on the Common. 

Once at the Common, protestors will be invited to engage with local groups and organizations at tables for information-sharing and grassroots strength building. You'll also be entertained by circus and street performers PLUS more music! We will celebrate the diversity that makes America shine! All flags welcome.

Together we call for justice, OUR Constitution to be upheld, and an end to executive overreach. We honor the flag of the United States, a symbol of freedom and national solidarity. We honor the rights of every person within its borders.

We are no longer interested in simply protesting the damage coming out of Washington, D.C., which affects every individual, we are here to stop it. As Martin Luther King Jr. said, "A time comes when silence is betrayal."  

We will not be silent, we will gather on the streets on June 14 and every day to follow in our neighborhoods, in collaboration. “The work of bringing people together in mutual recognition and cooperation is never really done”. --Archbishop Anthony Broglio

Co-hosted by Indivisible Brattleboro and Brattleboro Area Action, this partnership is bound by a shared commitment to nonviolence, inclusion, and democratic participation.

title: DAY OF ACTION TO DEFEND NATIONAL MONUMENTS + PUBLIC LANDS

location.venue: Your favorite national monument, national park, or other close-to-home public lands in New Mexico

description:
At Your Favorite National Monument

Background

In April, The Washington Post reported that the Trump administration has a short list of six national monuments they’re considering slashing: Baaj Nwaavjo I’tah Kukveni-Ancestral Footprints of the Grand Canyon (AZ), Ironwood Forest (AZ), Chuckwalla (CA), Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks (NM), Bears Ears (UT) and Grand Staircase-Escalante (UT). President Trump has already signed a proclamation opening up the Pacific Islands Heritage National Monuments to commercial fishing.

Public land advocates have a narrow window to push back and protect these and other places. In 2017, Trump led the largest rollback of public land protections in history, slashing Utah’s Bears Ears and Grand-Staircase Escalante national monuments by 85 and 47 percent, respectively. In response, nearly 3 million Americans rose up in protest.  Let’s build a loud community of public land defenders across the country. Let the Trump administration know these places are for the people - not billionaires or corporate polluters.   

What Success Looks Like

We hope this day of action will generate media attention at local, state and national levels with visuals of people uniting across some of our country’s most precious landscapes. Even small rallies with honed messaging in critical locations are effective. Additionally, a social media element that reaches voters across the country who support public lands will create a powerful message.

We invite all public land defenders to participate, whether that’s by posting a photo of their favorite trails to social on June 7 or showing up in person on the land with friends and family. 

How to Join

Gather a Group: Bring friends, family, or your organization members to your favorite national monument, national park, or other close-to-home public land.
View a list of BLM-managed National Monuments and Conservation Lands here.
View a list of National Park Service-managed national monuments and national parks in New Mexico here.
Before you go: If you invite a large group, call the land manager to see if a permit will be required for your expected group size or if there are any other considerations for First Amendment activities. Some monuments have designated First Amendment areas.

Make a homemade sign: Use example slogans or create your own.
"Not for Sale / No Se Vende"
“Protect Our Parks”
“Public Lands in Public Hands”
"Hands Off National Monuments"
"Protect Sacred Sites"
"Public Lands, Not Private Profit"
Take photos
Stand near a national monument sign, notable landmark or gorgeous view.
Show your signs clearly.
If you see signs of destruction and negative impacts from the DOGE firing spree (think: trash at trailheads, “closed” signs, etc), document them and report them to New Mexico Wild here.
Share online - and pass forward
Tag: #nmwild so we can share your photos!
Tag: #monumentsforall | #handsoff | #notforsale 
Tag: Sec. Burgum (@secretaryburgum) and your members of Congress (find your reps here)
Tag: 5 friends, nominating them to go to their favorite monument, park or other public land with a sign.
Sign and share the petition
Call your members of Congress at (202) 224-3121 and tell them to let the Trump administration know that these places are not for sale.
Who’s Invited to Join

Local residents
Tribal Nations & Indigenous advocates
Business owners
Outdoor recreationists (hikers, climbers, birders, campers)
Hunters & anglers
Conservation groups
Faith leaders
Artists & youth
YOU
Why This Matters

The Trump administration is dismantling our parks to sell them off to billionaires and big corporations. These actions will cut off access to national public lands and destroy wildlife habitats. Removing these monument protections is part of the broader scheme to sell off public lands - and Americans’ shared national heritage.

We say: Enough is enough. These lands are not for sale.

https://www.nmwild.org/event/june-7th-day-of-action-rally-for-your-public-lands/

title: Democracy Day Sioux Falls
description:
Democracy Day Sioux Falls
Political Rally in Support of Veterans
Food / Cash Donation Drive to support South Dakota DAV
Friday, June 6th, 2026 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm
12th & Kiwanis Sioux Falls SD

SIOUX FALLS, S.D. – A rally and food drive is planned for Friday, June 6, 2025. Community members are invited to gather for Democracy Day Sioux Falls from 5 to 7 p.m. at 12th Street and Kiwanis Avenue in Sioux Falls, in front of the Battleship Memorial. Rally goers to this bipartisan event are encouraged to bring signs showing their support, along with non-perishable food donations or money for veterans in need.
Non-perishable food items and cash donations will support local South Dakota DAV Arthur H. Muchow Chapter No.1. The DAV staff will deliver food to several veterans organizations around the city that help feed veterans in need.Those interested in donating but not able to stay for the rally will be able to drive through and drop off donations. A DAV trailer will be parked at the Battleship Memorial, for the duration of the event with volunteers available to accept donations.
This food drive is sponsored by local citizens in cooperation with the DAV. The last food rally April 19, at Van Eps Park, provided 3,400 lbs of food and raised over $4,000 for Feeding South Dakota. Permits have been obtained for the rally.
June 6 stands strong in American history as the invasion of Normandy in 1944, or D-Day. The U.S.S. South Dakota location was chosen because of the role that ship played in World War II.
“It’s appropriate to gather there on the anniversary of D-Day to demand better care and protections for our service members today,” organizers said. “The ship’s history includes changing its name to Battleship X to protect its identity in the Pacific theater. Because of its success in combat and defending freedom during World War II, it helped end the facist regime of the Axis Powers.”
"This event allows me the opportunity to support our country's real heroes, our veterans. I'm also here to support two of my personal heroes. My dad, a World War II veteran and my son, a VA healthcare provider. He specializes in the unique needs of combat veterans. Neither ever thought what they fought for and continut to fight for would be threatened by corruption from within. Save our democracy, get involved!" said Mary D., an attendee of past events.
The public is called to make an impact in awareness of the concerns of the community. For more information on volunteering or attending an event page is available on Facebook, find it by searching #DemocracyDaySiouxFalls
www.facebook.com/events/2439234963100362/
Volunteer sign up can be found at https://forms.gle/yU7XxgfwiAWog4TE8

title: Defending Veterans on D-Day

location.venue: Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium Parking Lot

description:
June 6, 2025, marks the 81st anniversary of D-Day, the day the Allied forces launched the biggest sea invasion with a singular goal: overthrow the fascists of Nazi Germany. This year, we will honor the many men who fought and died that day, and we will continue their fight – this time on America’s shores and in America’s streets.  On Friday, June 6, veterans and their allies will join once again for a rally in front of the Marin Veterans Memorial Auditorium.

This rally will take place on the same day as the primary gathering on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., as well as in state capitols, large cities and small towns. Veterans and military family members are being fired by the thousands from federal jobs. Their healthcare is being gutted. Their benefits are under siege. We rally to:

Defend veteran and military family member employment in the federal workforce;

title: Fri. 5/30 > Mass Pike Overpass Standout - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202), Westfield
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! About 8 of us tried it out on Friday, May 2, and around 17 of us came out on 5/16. What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's a full-size sidewalk on the west side, and a narrow sidewalk (kind of like the narrow sidewalk at Mountain Park Rd.) on the east side. 

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

title: No Kings Day "Die-In" at Waterfront Park, Burlington
description:
As part of No Kings event at Burlington Waterfront, we will stage a Die-In to demonstrate the lethal impact of T**** administration budget, program cuts, foreign policy, immigration policy, attacks on our Democracy, and its very existence on people and programs, in the US and around the world.

By lying, sitting, or standing still and quiet on the grass with our tombstone signs, we’ll show the actual health, safety, and life impacts the actions of the current administration is having on us and the world. After lying or sitting in silence (for at least 15 minutes, but maybe more depending on overall No Kings event schedule) we will rise and silently arrange our tombstones as a graveyard (they will have a small stake taped to them), to remain displayed for the rest of the day.

This type of protest was used effectively during the Vietnam war, the AIDS crisis, and five years ago at the birth of the Black Lives Matter movement. These have already been done in 2025 Utah and NYC at 50501 events. The photo above from the NYC protest shows how dramatic and educational this will be.

More details, including tombstone creation parties, timing, recommended dress, will be emailed to you as the June 14 day-long event shapes up. 

This is a peaceful and silent protest.

title: Visibility Brigade - Share our message near Mall 205
description:
We gather weekly and show a message to passing cars on high visibility areas like freeway overpasses. You can bring your own signs but they're not required. We raise some larger Indivisible banners and spell out a short message in 2 foot tall letters. Then, we stand and wave at passing cars and chat about the movement and anything else. We stay about 2 hours, covering some high traffic time like rush hour. It's an easy and fun way to spread your message and meet fellow activists.

This week's will be at the Market Street overpass of I-205. You can park on Market street nearby and walk at most 2 blocks up a gentle hill.

title: Single Payer Day of Action #HandsOffMedicaid
description:
C0-Hosted by Colorado Healthcare Coalition and Indivisible Durango

Join us at Buckley Park in Durango for a powerful day of action to win universal, comprehensive health care in Colorado, and protest cuts to Medicaid!

This local gathering is part of the National Day of Action for Single Payer Health Care, and we’re bringing our voices—and our feet—to the streets to demand a system that puts people over profits.

Let’s celebrate a major legislative win! Colorado bill SB25-045 was just signed, the first step to a universal healthcare system covering all Colorado residents! Next step, build a movement to pass a ballot initiative - we’ve done that before!

We will also discuss the current attacks on Medicaid, and likely impacts on tens of thousands of residents in Colorado’s CD3 alone (31% of CD3’s residents - 194,121 people - are on Medicaid/CHIP).

What to expect:
🥾 First, a rally and gathering at Buckley Park featuring local speakers and organizers with
📢 Updates on CO SB25-045 and Colorado’s campaign for statewide single payer health care and
🧠 Opportunities to plug into local and statewide organizing
✊ A march on sidewalks through downtown calling for health care justice

We’re building this with local activists and students who believe in health care as a human right. Whether you're a seasoned organizer or just learning about the issue, your voice and presence matter.

Find information about the National Day of Action here:
https://nationalsinglepayer.com/national-day-of-action/

title: Truth and Democracy Coalition Press Conference
description:
Truth and Democracy Coalition Launches New Website to Fight for Democracy, Counter Divisive Propaganda, and Defend the Constitution at https://TruthandDemocracyCoalition.com

Press Release May 17, 2025

Truth and Democracy Coalition Launches Campaign to Bring Americans Together Around Shared Values. Organizer Richard Procida Produces Programs Designed to Cross Ideological, Religious, and Political lines to Undermine False and Divisive Narratives.

The Truth and Democracy Coalition to hold a press Conference on March 30, 2025, at 1 pm PDT at Liberty Plaza in Whittier, and online on March 31st at 10 am at https://Tinyurl.com/TDCPressConference
LOS ANGELES, CA, May 17, 2025 /24-7PressRelease/ -- On March 30, 2025, at 1 pm PDT in person and on March 31st at 10 am online, Richard Procida will present The Truth and Democracy Coalition's new website, programs, and events designed to reach across ideological, religious, and political lines to build the movement to save democracy. The in-person press conference and community meeting will be at the Liberty Community Plaza at 14181 Telegraph Rd, Whittier, CA 90604-2554. Register for the online press conference at https://tinyurl.com/TDCPressConference

Americans are a propagandized people. Political extremism and the widespread dissemination of divisive propaganda have pitted Americans against one another. All sides have been propagandized. Everyone is impacted. Conservatives, liberals, and radicals all consume propaganda.

The Truth and Democracy Coalition is committed to protecting and strengthening democracy in an era of growing division and disinformation. We bring together individuals from all walks of life—Republicans and Democrats, radicals and moderates, Socialists, Liberals, and Conservatives—to uphold and defend the Constitution while strengthening the foundations of democracy. Our mission is to build a broad, diverse, and engaged movement that empowers individuals and communities to stand against authoritarian threats, defend democratic values, and promote truth in public discourse.

Richard Procida, the founder of the Truth and Democracy Coalition, will present the web page, explain the programs, and answer questions. He is available for media interviews and can be contacted at (562) 665-3317 and RichProcida64@Gmail.com

Author and attorney Richard Procida founded the Truth and Democracy Coalition to unite Americans, counter disinformation, defend the Constitution, and fight for democracy. His vision is to bring conservatives, liberals, and radicals together around shared values. Democracy, freedom, and the rule of law, for example, are foundational American values.

As an attorney who studied constitutional law at American University and authored a textbook on foreign comparative constitutional law, he intuitively recognized the looming threat to democracy and freedom posed by the propaganda war. At a time when many were saying that Trump was "just a symptom" of a larger racist system, Mr. Procida began writing and speaking at rallies calling for impeachment and warning Americans about the threat to democracy posed by the Trump Administration. He started a podcast called Democracy Under Fire which later became The Truth and Democracy Podcast, and wrote articles for LAProgressive.com, BuzzFlash.com, and DemCast.com. He held annual events on January 6th to remember the assault on the capital and prevent it from happening again.

Mr. Procida studied social science and communications with a minor in the Study of Women and Men in Society at the University of Southern California. He studied law at American University, Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C. He also co-authored a survey of laws and social attitudes toward sexually explicit materials in various countries and regions of the world (Social Issues in Global Perspective: Pornography, Lexington Books (2003)). He currently leads the Truth and Democracy Coalition.

title: No Kings Montgomery County PA

location.venue: Montgomery County Courthouse Steps Swede St

description:
Peaceful Protest at Montgomery County Courthouse Steps on Swede Street. Bring your Megaphone, Bring your noisemakers, Bring your signs. Be creative! Stand up, Fight Back!!

Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

💰 He’s using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party: Donald Trump’s birthday celebration is expected to cost millions of our tax dollars, all while Republicans claim there’s no money for Social Security, SNAP, or Medicaid.

👑 We are united against kings: Trump has already indicated that he’s aiming for at least a third term, and now he’s planning a self-aggrandizing military parade in D.C But the American people don’t put up with kings. Together, we will mobilize in huge numbers to reject this corruption and abuse of power—it’s in our DNA as a country.

✋ They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

We’re standing together against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption. On June 14, we gather to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!

This event is being brought to you by all of the Montgomery County Indivisible Groups:

Indivisible Greater Jenkintown
Indivisible Lower Merion
Indivisible MontCo PA & Friends
Indivisible Narberth & Beyond
Indivisible Upper Merion
Social Justice Indivisible

title: NO KINGS in Jackson, Michigan!
description:
On June 14th, President Trump is planning a massive military parade. This is a show of force comparable to those in China, Russia, North Korea -- **Trump is intentionally emulating the acts of tyrants. And he's doing it with our money!** Tens of millions of dollars are going to this display of power while the Trump administration and DOGE keep cutting services that we need.

But real power doesn't lie in militant control. Real power comes from the American people. **Real power comes from us!** 

Trump and DOGE keep trying to control us. They defund community and cultural services that keep us informed and bring us together -- libraries, museums, education, student aid, radio, television, the arts. They strip away protections and programs that protect the Earth, threatening our natural resources. They pull back the regulations keeping us safe on the job. They cut our ability to retire without worry. They rob us of emergency funding. They take away our Medicaid and CDC funding to put us in danger. 

And when we speak out? They punish us by kidnapping random people off the streets and sending them to suffer inhumane conditions -- deporting regardless of innocence or legal status. They block judges' ability to keep them in check. They even make it more and more difficult for us to vote!

These are the acts of a ruler trying to keep the people in check. **It's time for us to remind Trump that the U.S. is a democracy, not a monarchy.** Donald Trump is not a king!

NO KINGS!

June 14th, Withington Park, downtown Jackson MI. Come rally with us! 
Come when you can! **All are welcome!**

---
If your group is interested in attending or speaking at the protest, please contact organizer Ella Scott at ellascott41637@gmail.com to give a quick heads-up! We'd be happy to have you!

Please visit the information table when you arrive! Thank you!

WARNING FOR ATTENDEES: Please don't park in the Sew and Sew parking lot; you will be towed. Instead, park Tim Walberg's lot, the bank parking lot, or in the old Crossfit lot.

title: NO KINGS RALLY - MORRISTOWN
description:
📢 📢 Morristown Town Hall, 200 South St.📢 
11:00 AM - 12:30 PM
📢 Large crowds are expected. 📢 Carpool, use a ride share or public transportation. 📢 Stay together. 📢 Bring a fully charged phone; disable location services . 📢 There will be NO seating or public bathrooms. 📢 
Dress appropriately for the weather. 📢 Wear sunscreen and avoid umbrellas. 📢 Bring water. 

*WHAT IS “NO KINGS”?*

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political positions, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies. They think they rule—but we are bigger than even their worst aspirations.


*****PLEASE PARK LEGALLY and obey all signs. Parking will be a challenge, Carpool, rideshare, or use public transportation. There are several public parking lots in Morristown, including the lot behind Town Hall on Franklin St. DO NOT park in the Kings shopping lot. 
For your safety, cross only at crosswalks. South Street is a busy road. *
. 
📢 📢 Remember, this is a PEACEFUL protest; do not engage with counter protestors or agitators. 📢 📢 

Be respectful and dispose of any trash properly before leaving the rally; keep Morristown beautiful!!

📢 📢 📢 On June 14th, join us as we show up where he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, NO KINGS! Bring your signs and your voice and meet us at 200 South Street in Morristown at 11:00 AM. We'll have music and speakers and will remind the world what democracy really looks like. 

📢 📢 📢 June 14th isn't about Donald Trump. It is Flag Day and the flag belongs to us.  NO KINGS Morristown is hosted by the Morris County Democratic Committee, Planned Parenthood Action Fund of NJ, NJ 11th for Change and New Jersey Citizen Action.

No Kings is a nationwide day of defiance. From city blocks to small towns, from courthouse steps to community parks, we’re taking action to reject authoritarianism. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind should not be brought to events.

title: NO KINGS Leland, NC | Indivisible

location.venue: Intersection of Olde Waterford Way & Route 17 Southbound

description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**

NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. They’ve defied our courts, deported Americans, disappeared people off the streets, attacked our civil rights, and slashed our services. 

🚨**On June 14th, we’re showing up to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**🚨

This event is hosted by Indivisible Defenders of Democracy (Brunswick County), Indivisible Wilmington, and Brunswick Indivisible Stepping Forward for Action.

Join us at the intersection of Olde Waterford Way and Route 17 Southbound between the hours of 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM. 

Rain or shine, we will stand on the grass near this high-traffic intersection. Our job is to be visible. Our aim is to be respectful, safe, and considerate of passing motorists.

**Please park in the public parking areas near the Harris Teeter at 2021 Olde Regent Way, Leland, NC 28451. From there, it is a 5-minute walk to the intersection of Olde Waterford Way and Route 17 Southbound. Look for the Wells Fargo Bank on the corner.**

BRING: Big, legible signs with messages related to the No Kings theme. American flags. A backpack with food and water, sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, an umbrella. Feel free to bring a chair to sit a spell if you get tired. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

Please Note: There is a NO KINGS Rally in Wilmington at Innes Park (102 N. 3rd St.) from 12:00 PM - 1:30 PM hosted by Women Organizing for Wilmington. We encourage you to attend whichever is most convenient– or both, if you're feeling ambitious!

Check out nokings.org for more information.
accessibility_notes: There are many retail establishments within close walking distance where you can make use of restrooms. There are some shade trees where you can step out of the sun to rest. Parking lots are within walking distance. There is a Novant facility on this corner that is closed on Saturdays which means the parking lot will be empty.

description:

 🎉 Freedom & Democracy Protest — Join us as we raise our voices alongside the City of Santa Clarita’s anticipated annual Fourth of July Fireworks Show! 🎆 As the sky lights up over Valencia Town Center, we’ll stand together in purpose and celebration — reminding our community that Independence Day is not just about fireworks, but about defending the values that make democracy real. 

Let’s close out the holiday with joy, unity, and a clear message: we’ll have a Republic — if we can keep it.  🎉

☀️ DOUBLE THE GOOD TROUBLE ☀️ - Make your voices be heard.

Join Indivisible CA27 for a powerful Independence and post–Independence Day visibility protests as we reclaim the meaning of freedom, democracy, and justice in America.  Pride in our FLAG, proud to be FREE.  ☀️ Before it gets too hot!!! ☀️

Right before the fireworks or While the fireworks fade the next day, our message will rise: real independence means defending everyone’s rights — voting rights, reproductive freedom, LGBTQ+ dignity, climate justice, immigrant protections, and civil liberties for all.

title: Independence Day Resistance Rally - Indivisible - Democracy Action Network
description:
"No Kings Since 1776" - Standing Against Autocracy

Join us on July 5th for a peaceful march and rally to reaffirm our commitment to democratic principles and stand against the threats of autocracy. As we gather just after Independence Day, we honor our founders' revolutionary spirit and their rejection of monarchical rule.

Why July 5th?

While the nation celebrates on the 4th, we gather the day after to remind ourselves that independence isn't just a historical achievement—it's an ongoing responsibility. Just as the revolutionaries of 1776 declared "No More Kings," we continue their legacy by standing vigilant against autocratic tendencies in our own time.

What to Bring:

- Signs (suggested themes: democratic values, checks and balances, "No Kings Since 1776")
- Water and sun protection
- Your commitment to peaceful democratic action

This non-partisan event welcomes all who believe in preserving democratic institutions and opposing autocratic governance, regardless of political affiliation.

title: Protest Elon Musk's Illegal Government Takeover #TeslaTakedown - Stanford Saturdays
description:
PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest on the sidewalk in front of the Stanford Tesla showroom. There will be theatrics and dancing. Get ready to improv! We'll also be looping through Stanford Shopping Mall with peaceful positive energy. Of course you may opt out and continue to demonstrate in front of the Tesla showroom. 

We know making lots of noise is typically part of a good protest. But most protests aren’t right across the street from a Ronald McDonald House. Let’s take care to keep our noise levels down to a dull roar. Bring your energy and spirit, but let’s refrain from the cowbells, drums and car honks. We can get our point across without interfering with our neighbors on the other side of the road.

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations! Signs, flags, and similar items are welcome.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police and mall security, including if we are asked to leave. By the way, we have already have a fantastic relationship with mall security, which is a plus!

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

#BoycottTesla #DivestFromTesla

title: Unite For Veterans, Unite for America Rally/Protest
description:
Rally With America’s Veterans
America made a promise to its veterans. It's a promise we intend to keep.
On June 6th, join thousands of veterans, military families, and their allies across the country and on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., for the Unite for Veterans, Unite for America Rally. We will have a local event in Greene Co, Ohio in solidarity with the DC event. It will be from 4-6pm at in Beavercreek. Register to attend and for information. 

We are coming together to defend the benefits, jobs, and dignity that every generation of veterans has earned through sacrifice.

Veteran jobs, healthcare, and essential VA services are under attack. We will not stand by.

Why We Rally from Unite For Veterans

Veterans and military family members are being fired by the thousands from federal jobs. Our healthcare is being gutted. Our benefits are under siege.

This isn't the first time veterans have had to fight for what was promised. From the Bonus Army of 1932 to the battles for the GI Bill and Agent Orange care, veterans have always led the charge for justice.

Now, it's our turn.

We rally to:

Defend veteran and military family member employment in the federal workforce

Stop the privatization and weakening of the Department of Veterans Affairs

Hold political leaders accountable for policies that harm veterans and their families

title: Unite for Veterans, Unite for America
description:
On June 6, 2025, veterans, patriots, and supporters will gather in Houston under the banner of 50501-Houston to honor the legacy of D-Day and to protest in defense of the U.S. Constitution, stand up for veterans' rights, and demand full support for those who have served.

The rally will call on the Federal Government to rehire wrongfully terminated employees and to fully fund and implement the PACT Act, a historic piece of legislation that directly affects the health and well-being of veterans exposed to toxic substances during military service.

“This is more than a protest—it’s a movement of accountability and unity,” organizers said. “We stand for the Constitution, we stand for veterans, and we will not be silent.”

What Is the PACT Act?
The Sergeant First Class (SFC) Heath Robinson Honoring Our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act is the most significant expansion of VA health care and benefits in decades. It ensures that veterans exposed to toxic substances—including burn pits, Agent Orange, and radiation—receive the care and compensation they deserve.

Key Provisions of the PACT Act Include:

Expanded eligibility for VA health care for veterans of Vietnam, Gulf War, and post-9/11 eras

20+ new “presumptive conditions” linked to toxic exposure

Automatic coverage for conditions like cancers and respiratory illnesses

Required toxic exposure screenings for all enrolled veterans

Additional funding for VA research, staffing, and treatment systems

Veterans are encouraged to file claims now and check their eligibility for new or expanded benefits under this law.

Why This Matters:
Tens of thousands of veterans are affected by toxic exposures. Without full funding and government follow-through, the promises made by the PACT Act could fall short. That’s why 50501-Houston is calling on all Americans to unite on June 6—to honor those who fought for freedom and fight now for those living with the aftermath of service.

title: United For Veterans, United For America Rally/Protest
description:
This is a local event in solidarity with Rally With America’s Veterans 

America made a promise to its veterans. It's a promise we intend to keep.

We will have a local event in Greene Co, Ohio in solidarity with the DC event. It will be from 4-6pm at in Beavercreek. Register to attend and for information. 

We are coming together to defend the benefits, jobs, and dignity that every generation of veterans has earned through sacrifice.

Veteran jobs, healthcare, and essential VA services are under attack. We will not stand by.

Why We Rally from Unite For Veterans

Veterans and military family members are being fired by the thousands from federal jobs. Our healthcare is being gutted. Our benefits are under siege.

This isn't the first time veterans have had to fight for what was promised. From the Bonus Army of 1932 to the battles for the GI Bill and Agent Orange care, veterans have always led the charge for justice.

Now, it's our turn.

We rally to:

Defend veteran and military family member employment in the federal workforce

Stop the privatization and weakening of the Department of Veterans Affairs

Hold political leaders accountable for policies that harm veterans and their families

title: Wheeler Salmonberry Trail Ground Building
description:
**Join The Salmonberry Trail in our exciting ground breaking event at Waterfront Park in Wheeler!**

The City of Wheeler is excited to announce that we are taking the first steps toward revitalization of Wheeler’s section of the Salmonberry Trail through partnership with the Salmonberry Trail Foundation and Tillamook Coast Visitors Association. We will be holding a **Ground Building event and ceremony on July 12, 2025 from 1:00-5:00 PM.** We truly could not be more excited for the recreational opportunities this trail will provide for our community.

This transformative project holds the potential to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits to our community. By linking the Willamette Valley to the Coast, it will not only strengthen regional connectivity but also invigorate rural tourism and empower small businesses. It champions public health and safe, active transportation options while expanding equitable access to the outdoors for all residents. Most importantly, it lays the foundation for sustainable infrastructure that will support our economy, environment, and quality of life for generations to come.

We will have local vendors, music, games, and a ribbon cutting ceremony celebrating the beginning of this coastal section of the trail. 
- July 12th, 1PM - 5PM
- Waterfront Park (500 Marine Dr, Wheeler, OR 97147)

---
**ABOUT THE SALMONBERRY TRAIL**
The Salmonberry Trail is an 82-mile multi-use path transforming a historic rail line into Oregon’s next big adventure. Connecting communities from the Willamette Valley to the coast, the trail will provide safe routes for recreation and education, expand economic opportunities, and improve public health. In partnership with local organizations, it will offer unique educational programs while promoting outdoor activity and conservation, making it a cornerstone of community development and environmental stewardship across the state.

**Wheeler Demonstration Project – Salmonberry Trail**
The Wheeler Demonstration Project is a short, high-impact segment of the Salmonberry Trail located in downtown Wheeler. This 1,800-foot trail segment runs north from Rector Street, across Hemlock Street, and along the bay side of the Oregon Coast Scenic Railway tracks adjacent to Botts Marsh. It features a compacted gravel path for pedestrians, designed to enhance safety and encourage walking in the downtown area.
Developed in partnership with the City of Wheeler, Oregon Coast Scenic Railway, Lower Nehalem Community Trust, and the Salmonberry Trail Foundation, the project supports local economic activity, offers environmental education through interpretive signage, and provides a model for similar efforts in other communities along the trail corridor.

title: Weekly Rally at Orange Plaza Square Park - When We Unite, We Win!
description:
**Come to the Orange Plaza Square Park each week**, rain or shine, to take a stand opposing the oligarchs, billionaires and the regime that's attacking our way of life and the Constitution of the USA. Join our community in a nonviolent, peaceful demonstration! Make your voice heard. We are the many, they are the few that want to rule us all. Take a stand for democracy. Bring your signs, bring pots and pans, your whistles and kazoos and meet at the fountain - we'll spread out from there after a safety briefing. Let the people be heard! Let’s make some noise!

**GENERAL PROTEST/RALLY REMINDERS**

Remember the ABCs of protesting:

A) Always obey traffic signals and directions of the safety team!

B) Beware of detractors*! Do not talk to detractors or unaffiliated interviewers - doing so increases risks for all of us, including all the volunteers and organizers.

C) Chill vibes please! Never touch anyone else or their property (e.g., car, sign, backpack) without permission. Have fun! Build community!

*As our events become more popular, we may attract detractors and Trump/Elon/MAGA supporters, either passing in cars or as rally attendees. Some of their tactics are to act friendly, ask questions, and pretend to care about your answers. They may also gesture, yell, name-call, and use foul language. They often look to get a reaction they can capture on video. Do NOT engage with or speak to them. Do NOT answer their questions. Do NOT yell back at them or gesture (thumbs down, middle finger, etc.) Do NOT post photos or videos of them online. Do NOT reveal any personal or contact info to anyone at this or any rally you do not know to be on your side. If someone becomes threatening or violent, move away quickly and alert a safety volunteer, a police officer, and/or call 911. These guidelines keep you, our volunteers, and our organizers safe. Thank you!

**[Learn to de-escalate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Pgmn9QRr48&list=PLqIrQkVlKU3RZw0ytVd3U7XS3ofAaZItu&index=2)**

**[Learn to Grey-rock](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/grey-rock-method)**

**MEET YOUR HOST**

**[Indivisible CA 40](https://linktr.ee/indivisibleca40)** is a non-partisan, all volunteer grassroots group of residents in the CA-40 congressional district who are holding elected officials accountable, from city councils and school boards all the way up to Congress. We partner with other community organizations to uplift and support our neighbors while we work toward electoral change in 2026.
