title: NO KINGS Mankato
description:
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

Join us in Mankato Saturday, June 14, from 11-12:30 pm to say:

We are united against kings.

No using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party.

They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

LOGISTICS

We will rally on the sidewalks along two busy side streets in Mankato, Warren St and South Broad St: north on Broad from Warren to Cherry, and 1-2 blocks east and west of Broad on Warren. 

Based on attendance, we will extend the rally in those 3 directions, following the guidance of rally leaders.

Volunteers will assist participants with logistical information and support on rally sidewalks rather than at a central location.

Please use legal, public parking only. Consider arriving by 10:30 to park and find your place. If able, please use parking ramps and walk. Free municipal ramps include Mankato Place, Civic Center, Second Street, and City Center ramps. The last one is the garage along Riverfront Drive between Cherry and Warren streets.

Bring a sign or two, water, cash for emergencies, and weather-appropriate clothing. The nearest bathrooms are a couple of blocks away, so be prepared for that too.

SAFETY

A core principle behind all NO KINGS events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. We ask participants to obey traffic and other laws and be mindful of pedestrians using the sidewalks. There will be a police presence at the event but we will rely on our own peacekeepers, volunteers, and you to assist with de-escalation. If asked by leaders or police to disperse, please do so at once.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible St. Peter/Greater Mankato and ACLU MN and COPAL MN. Thank you so much for standing with us!

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Food Insecurity
description:
Please join us for our 13th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday May 31st, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be on Food Insecurity.

Food insecurity is when people don't have enough to eat and don't know where their next meal will come from. It's a big problem in the United States, where about 47 million people, including about 14 million children, experience food insecurity annually. 

You can be food insecure if you worry about running out of food, are not able to afford balanced meals, or you eat less or skip meals.

People disproportionately impacted by food insecurity include children, many communities of color, households with low incomes, immigrant communities, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, people in certain geographies (e.g., rural areas, cities, the South), people who are formerly incarcerated, and single-parent households and many elderly.

Food insecurity exists in every county and congressional district in the U.S.

 Key strategies to address food insecurity include strengthening Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), making free school meals available to all children, expanding access to affordable housing and healthcare, and reducing food waste.   

This is the exact OPPOSITE of what the current administration is doing!!!

Our guest speaker will be Linda Hutchings, the Food Sourcing Manager for Community Food Rescue, a nonprofit organization in Danbury, CT, that works to eliminate hunger in the Greater Danbury area. She is also a key figure in the Community Action Agency of Western Connecticut's efforts to combat food insecurity. Hutchings plays a crucial role in connecting food pantries with food sources, managing food drives, and developing new food banks. She has been instrumental in rescuing food from local stores and partnering with local companies to provide food to those in need. 

Live music will be performed by Erik Rabaska.
Erik Rabasca is a musician, producer, singer/songwriter, founder of the band Light Warriors and the independent label Highest Frequency Records. He plays a fusion of styles as an acoustic soloist ranging from folk, roots and jazz to reggae, indie and even a touch of country. His songwriting has been compared to Bob Dylan and Marley, Paul Simon and more. He has toured the country, performed internationally, opened for Grammy-winners Jon Batiste and Mike Farris, reggae legends Mad Professor, Culture, Sugar Minott, among others, has collaborated with Mad Professor and released over a dozen albums and EPs in various projects (Light Warriors, Lions Gate, Ecstatica, Human Tribes Collective, Other Planes of There, cuebrane) over the last six years alone. He is currently playing in and around the Hudson Valley, NYC and CT. Light Warriors are Ambassadors as part of WhyHunger’s Artists Against Hunger Poverty program.

As part of the Connecticut Hope Collective,  Erik wrote and recorded a song about food insecurity called,  "Just Get To It".  This track was written with the intention of serving some good in the world. 100% of sales will go toward the benefit of the local charity associated through the Pass The Guitar series of concerts. These events bring together 20+ songwriters to raise money for local CT organizations that support hunger and homelessness.

https://theconnecticuthopecollective.bandcamp.com/track/just-get-to-it

The Connecticut Hope Collective is a group of musicians and songwriters who collaborate to create music and events that support local organizations and communities in need. They aim to bring people together and raise awareness for issues like hunger and homelessness while promoting a sense of hope and community. 

The rally is non-partisian. All are welcome.

There will be something for everyone. We'll have speakers, we'll rally with our signs, we'll take a short march and we'll have live music. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week.  Since our theme this week is food insecurity, please be extra generous if you can and help us fill the bins at our local food pantry.  

Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but 
some special requests from the food pantry include:

-  Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

-   Individually packaged items. so if you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

-  Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

-  SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

- 11:00 - 11:15  Assemble and rally at curb (You are welcome to arrive prior to 11:00 for extra curb time)

- 11:15 - 11:45  Speaker(s)

- 11:45 - Noon  Rally at curb with chant leader

- Noon - 12:20  March with chant leader

- 12:20.              Closing Song

- 12:30.              Disperse

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally.  We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking.  It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting,  marching, themes with speakers,  live music,  fun trinkets, sign making.  We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️ 

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square, is behind the municipal center (number 1 on the map you will receive after registration). PT Barnum Square is the triangle shaped area to the far right on the map and in the center of the map.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please do not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊

title: NO KINGS
description:
Let’s unite to defend our Constitution and push back against the troubling direction our country is heading!

We reject efforts to normalize displays of power meant to intimidate rather than inspire. Instead, we stand for a democracy rooted in compassion, transparency, and collective action. No Kings means no to fascism, no to fear, and yes to a future where people come before politics.

Right now, Congress is working on a bill that would take healthcare away from millions of people but still give billionaires more tax breaks. It’s a clear example of unfair priorities that hurt everyday families while helping the richest get richer.

We believe healthcare is a human right. We believe in a democracy that serves the people, not the powerful. And we believe it’s our responsibility to rise up and defend those principles.

Please bring a non-perishable food item to support our local food pantry—because community care and mutual aid are acts of resistance!

Join us in solidarity. Together, we’ll show that we will not be silenced, we will not be intimidated, and we will never stop fighting for justice and dignity for all!

title: Roadside Rallies Against Fascism
description:
Join us for another Roadside Rally Against Fascism down in Bellmawr at the corner of Black Horse Pike and E Browning Road. 

There is a good amount of traffic and plenty of sidewalk, and there should be parking available on nearby residential streets (make sure not to obstruct the nearby police and fire departments on Lewis Ave). We would love to welcome as many folks as possible to come make some noise with us! 

This is a nonviolent demonstration, so please attend with safety and de-escalation in mind. We do not expect any counterprotestors, but we can never be 100% sure. Do your best to minimize engagement with hecklers, and don't be too shy to smile and wave at our supporters!

Please bring your signs, flags, street antics, and any other ways you can think of to joyfully disturb the peace. But please avoid any messaging that is outright hateful, violent, or discriminatory.

See you out there!

title: Friday Rally to Protect Democracy in Honor of Our Veterans in Mentor
description:
Come on over to Eleanor Garfield Park in Mentor Friday from 10-11:30am. 

We rally every Friday, but this week's event will be in honor of our veterans.    

June 6th marks the 81st anniversary of D-Day.  

Veterans are planning a massive rally in Washington, D.C., and elsewhere on June 6 to protest cuts at the Department of Veterans Affairs and call for the protection of veterans' benefits and jobs, which are being hurt by the Trump administration's efforts to reduce the size of the federal government.

We will gather in solidarity with veterans.  We will stand along Mentor Avenue with signs and flags. We will peacefully show that we object to the insidious cuts to vital federal programs and employees.

District 14 members will have the opportunity to fill out comment sheets for Congressman Dave Joyce.

Bring signs, friends, and family. Bring family-friendly signs.

We will be donating food to the Geauga County Veteran's Food Pantry.  Please check their website for items they need:

www.geaugacountyveteranfoodpantry.com

Donating is optional.

Please park in the lower lot if you are able to make the walk up to the event site. Please keep the spaces in the upper lot open for those who need a shorter walk.

This event is sponsored by Ohio District 14 Partners in collaboration with the pro-democracy groups in Ohio's District 14.

Note—this event was formerly titled ‘Where’s Congressman Joyce.” Though the title has changed, we still wonder where he is, and why he is not answering our specific concerns.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Moral Mondays with Sacramento Poor People’s Campaign
description:
**Join the Sacramento Poor People's Campaign: **
**Mondays June 9, 16, and 23 12-1 pm**

**June 9th and 16th -  Federal Court House at 5th and I   
June 23rd - ICE Building at 7th and Capitol Mall. **
 
June 9 -  focus is on the effects of the administration’s proposed budget cuts on low-income communities.

June 16 - focus is on the environmental impact of the administration’s attacks on programs and regulations which protect our planet, public lands and parks, and climate.

June 23 - focus is on immigration and civil rights at the Federal Court 

Since the time of the first Trump administration, the Poor People’s Campaign has organized and aroused tens of thousands of people through Moral Monday events, a national initiative led by faith leaders, progressives, advocates, and community members dedicated to social justice. Bishop Barber, one of the founders, was recently arrested at the Capitol in DC.
 
The Sacramento Moral Mondays in 2025 will not include direct actions. But it will serve as a response to severe budget cuts, the dismantling of rights, and unjust policies at the local, state, and national levels. Each event will take place at a central location in Sacramento, providing an opportunity for the community to come together and advocate for the restoration of "morality" in the public sphere. Each Monday will serve as a platform for unity, pushing back against false narratives, harmful policies, and misguided perceptions of democracy in our state.
 
Cathleen Williams,
Sacramento Poor People’s Campaign (Sac PPC)

By signing up to this event, you will receive communications from the Sacramento Poor People’s Campaign.

title: Tues. 6/10 > I-91 Overpass Standout - 9 Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

title: NO TYRANTS London, Ontario
description:
**In Canada, we don’t put up with tyrants. In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.** So, let’s stand in solidarity with people all over the world who despise dictators, oligarchs, and authoritarianism.

**NO TYRANTS/NO KINGS** is a Nationwide Day of Defiance, a mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. This is bigger than politics. They’ve defied courts, deported citizens, disappeared people off the streets, attacked civil rights, slashed essential services, and handed billions to their allies. **Enough is enough!**

LONDON, Ontario is STEPPING UP and saying **NO TYRANTS** in solidarity with Americans at home and abroad, 50501, Indivisible Abroad, Democrats Abroad, concerned Canadians, and a coalition of pro-democracy allies around the world. 
https://www.nokings.org/partners

On Saturday, June 14 — Flag Day in the US — Donald Trump wants tanks in the street and a made-for-TV display of dominance for his birthday. A spectacle meant to look like strength… but Donald Trump will NOT hijack the flag that day or ANY day. It belongs to Americans! The Canadian flag and CANADA don’t belong to him — ELBOWS UP, Canadians!

ON THIS FLAG DAY, we’re taking to the streets in Canada, the U.S… EVERYWHERE. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind. Check out nokings.org or indivisible.org for more information.

We will gather at the Victoria Park NW Gate at Richmond and Central (please show up a bit earlier). At the event's start time, we will march south around the park and past City Hall, then back to the gates of the park. There, we will have a rally showing London’s commitment to democracy and the combined power of We the People and We the North.

Craft a sign that shares YOUR message. Costumes welcome! Bring your acoustic instrument and your favourite freedom protest / anti-tyrant song!

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

See you there!

title: Fund Oregon Now: Rally to Demand a Budget That Puts People First
description:
## Rally with Us: Fund Oregon Now
🗓 **Thursday, June 5** | 🕛 **12:00 PM** | 📍 **Oregon State Capitol – 900 Court St NE, Salem, OR 97301**

Oregon’s **Democratic supermajority** was elected to fight for _us_. But right now, crucial programs that keep our communities **housed**, **healthy**, **fed**, and **safe** are on the chopping block—and working families are being left behind.

We’re gathering at the Capitol to say: **enough**.

### This moment is a test of values—and an opportunity to show that Oregon will not cower to pressure from wealthy special interests or lawmakers willing to gut vital services.

#### We must rise to meet it.

✊ We’re rallying for a budget that:

- Keeps Oregonians in their **homes** and food on the table
- Protects and **expands** access to healthcare
- Invests in **climate resilience** and a livable future
- Supports **working families**—not wealthy donors

### Why Now?
While **billionaires** glide through economic downturns, everyday people are being told to tighten their belts. Support for **housing**, **healthcare**, and **food assistance** is being threatened.

We’ve been told there’s no choice—but there is.

**Economists agree**: the best way to weather tough times is to _invest_ in communities. Oregon has a chance to lead with **courage** and **compassion**—not cuts and cowardice. We need lawmakers who are brave enough to say no to austerity politics and yes to the people who sent them to Salem.

That’s why we need you on the Capitol steps—_now_.

#### Tell our lawmakers:
We deserve better.
We demand better.
**Fund Oregon Now.**

Bring your voice, your signs, and your people.
This is our moment to **Protect Oregon Now**.

title: NO KINGS Citizens' Parade - Wilmington, Delaware
description:
Hosted by Indivisible Highlands and Beyond; co-hosted with 302 United and Delaware Working Families Power.

Come out for Wilmington’s "No Kings Citizens' Parade" as part of the June 14th National Day of Defiance to counter Trump's ridiculous $45 million birthday parade in DC on this same day. Join us as we parade down Wilmington's own Pennsylvania Avenue to say "NO KINGS!"

June 14th is Flag Day and also the 250th birthday of the army — a day that marks when Americans first organized to stand up to a king. "Trump isn’t honoring that legacy. He’s hijacking it to celebrate himself."

“This country doesn’t belong to a king — and we’re not letting him throw himself a parade funded by tens of millions of our taxpayer dollars while stealing from us and stripping away our rights, our freedoms, and the programs our families rely on. On June 14th, we’re coming together to send one clear message: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.”

We will gather at the corner of Pennsylvania Avenue and N. Bancroft Parkway in Wilmington. Specifically, we'll meet on grass lawn between the two sides of N. Bancroft Parkway - on the Wawaset Park side of PA Ave., between PA Ave. and W. 11th St. - and march/walk on the sidewalk along Pennsylvania Avenue toward Tower Hill School.

A short rally (with music and guest speakers) will precede the parade. The full roundtrip march is 1.3 miles long.

Bring flags and signs (two-sided, if possible) as well as kazoos, drums, cowbells, etc.

If walking isn't possible for you, please come anyway - with signs and flags - and be part of a Honk and Wave rally along Pennsylvania Ave.

Parking is available on N. Bancroft Parkway and surrounding streets.

Given our commitment to nonviolent action, we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. If you encounter a heckler or counter-protester (organized or unorganized, from a simple raised finger to a verbal taunt), the rule of thumb is to IGNORE IT!! Do not engage. If necessary, simply turn your back - or walk away.
accessibility_notes: If walking isn't possible for you, please come anyway - with signs and flags - and be part of a Honk and Wave rally along Pennsylvania Ave.

title: No Kings, Community Action Fair, March, Protest.
description:
Indivisible Bend, 50501 Central Oregon, Indivisible Sisters, and the Deschutes Youth Climate Coalition bring you a Nationwide call to action...

Agenda for Saturday, June 14th:

3- 4:30 pm Gather in Drake Park

4:30 March to Peace Corner

Performers and speakers on the stage Local organizations representing direct impacts to our
community.
Action booths, including protest sign making and Project Mail
Storm.
Kid friendly activities, including a Kazoo workshop.
Banned books Give away!
Drop in anytime you are able!
4:30 pm March to Peace Corner for peaceful protest.
Bring your signs or make one with us! NO KINGS!

What to expect...
NO KINGS! Community Action Fair, March, and Peaceful Protest!
50501 Central Oregon, Indivisible Bend and Deschutes Youth Climate Coalition invite you to our community event on Saturday, June 14th, as we join together to stand up against the authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. He is using our tax dollars to throw himself a military parade while slashing critical services, defying our courts, deporting and disappearing people and enriching his billionaire allies and together we are standing up saying ENOUGH!
We are outraged that:
Civil rights are being attacked. 
Costs are skyrocketing. 
People are being abducted and disappeared. 
Essential services are being gutted.
Free speech is threatened.
 Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute- we have NO KINGS in America!
Whatever disturbs you the most, this day is for you. Together, we stand against the abuses of power, cruelty, and corruption. Together, we rally to remind Trump and his enablers: America has No King!
Saturday, June 14th, we will assemble in Drake Park for a family-friendly display of community impact and action items all of us can participate in to ensure our voices are heard. Following this will be a short march from Drake Park to Peace Corner for a peaceful protest.

title: National Single Payer / HANDS OFF Medicaid Day of Action
description:
Presented by
Longmont Leads with Love, Longmont Area Democrats,
and Colorado Foundation for Universal Healthcare —
NATIONAL SINGLE PAYER / HANDS OFF MEDICAID DAY OF ACTION:


On the heels of the historic passage of Colorado’s SB25-045: Health-Care Payment System Analysis (Governor Polis signed SB25-045 into law on May 14) — alongside the egregious measures to strip millions of Americans, including children, OFF of life saving Medicaid, and the closure of already struggling rural hospitals, doing irreparable harm to rural communities —

Single payer universal healthcare WARRIORS are putting our broken healthcare system ON NOTICE, with a day of ACTION! SHOW UP! #HandsOffMedicaid

IDEAS FOR PROTEST SIGNS:

    Health Care Not Wealth Care
    Corporate-Run Health Insurance is Killing Us
    Hands Off Medicaid
    Cut Medicaid and Taxes for Billionaires?  WTF America?
    Liberty and Health Care Justice for All 
    Health Care Justice is Social Justice
    Imagine Being Free from Fear of Medical Debt
    72 Countries Have Universal Health Care, WTF America?

From the National Single Payer website:

Demand Healthcare Not “Wealthcare”!

We call on communities across the country to join in a National Day of Action on Saturday, May 31, 2025, to put National Single Payer Healthcare on the nation’s agenda. 

Our health care system is broken beyond repair. Insurance companies and for-profit middlemen create barriers to care and massive administrative waste. These result in unnecessary suffering and deaths. For over 60 years, piecemeal reforms have resulted in higher costs and the worst health outcomes among comparable nations.

We demand the recognition by our government that health care is a human right.

We demand the enactment of a publicly financed, national  single payer program that would provide comprehensive coverage to everyone.

The National Day of Action will bring people together locally and nationally from neighborhoods, unions, faith groups, businesses, and all types of civic organizations to focus our collective anger at corporate health insurers to bring real reform: put National Single Payer on the nation’s agenda!

title: NO KINGS Un-Parade Fairport

location.venue: All along W. Church St. toward Perinton Park
address_lines: West Church Street & South Main Street

description:
NO KINGS UN-PARADE FAIRPORT, NY
 
GRIT—Greater Rochester Integrity and Truth—is joining the national No Kings Day movement in a nationwide day of protest — and we’re taking it to the burbs. Rather than marching, our Un-Parade protest will take the form of peaceful parade watching along traditional parade routes in suburbs and small towns across Monroe County. Sitting in protest is a poignant symbol, directly taking issue with Trump’s irresponsible use of taxpayer dollars, his defiance of the constitution, and his trampling of our rights. An Un-Parade also allows people of differing physical abilities and all ages to participate.

#Details for Fairport
Time: 10am–12pm
Address: W. Church Street 
We will set up our chairs (or stand) starting at the intersection of West Church St and Main St and extend along W. Church St lining the street all the way to the canal (Perinton Park).

#Suggested Parking: 
Potter Park, at the corner of Potter Place and West Church St or on available side streets along West Church St. Please DO NOT PARK AT FAIRPORT VILLAGE LANDING, which is for the Farm Market and businesses. Carpool if you can.

#Not in Fairport? 
No worries, we are organizing in Pittsford, Brighton*, Webster, Henrietta… if you don’t see your town, and you want to help organize a No Kings Un-Parade, let us know: grit.roc@gmail.com

#Want to Volunteer? 
We need marshals and point people for burbs and villages and towns we haven’t yet signed up. Reach out to us at grit.roc@gmail.com. Be sure to let us know what you’re interested in and what town you’re in.

GRIT is a local group that meets twice a month in person to share knowledge, foster action, and come together as a community to help each other navigate and push back against the current administration. 

By registering for this event, it helps us know how many marshals and helpers we’ll need to have on site to ensure this a safe, peaceful event. And should any details change, it gives us an opportunity to keep you informed. Thank you for understanding. 

*Note — 50501 Rochester chapter is the lead for the Brighton protest; GRIT will be in charge of a specific area reserved for our “Un-Parade”. In other words, GRIT will have its own space for those who don’t want to march but want to protest with lawn chairs and protest signs. In this way, we can be more inclusive to those living in Brighton. Details on exactly where to line up and park in the 12 Corners will be forthcoming. If you want to participate in the Brighton protest, please sign up at https://www.nokings.org/#map. And, if you prefer to march, you can do that too. Win Win. Plus, we’re excited that we can collaborate with this group. Together we’re stronger!

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.
accessibility_notes: Public parking at Potter Park and side streets. There is no march or speakers, just peaceful protesting, showing proof to our community that we stand united against #47.

title: D-Day 81st Anniversary Protest
description:
This Friday June 6th is the 81st anniversary of D-Day. It will be a day of peaceful protest to commemorate the sacrifices of D-Day veterans, and to defend the US Constitution from threats to Democracy — the very democracy our D-Day veterans fought so hard to protect.

The protest is inspired by the “Bonus Army of 1932,” which marched on Washington in the summer of 1932 to successfully persuade politicians to re-instate promised WWI combat bonuses. Just like the Bonus Army of 1932, this Friday’s protests around the country, and on the Burnsville NC Square, will bring the threat of vanishing veterans’ rights to the forefront.

President Donald J. Trump is making quick work of erasing the history and benefits of millions of veterans. Trump’s announcement to rename “Veteran’s Day” to “Victory Day for WWI,” erases the very history of millions of veterans who served after WWI—specifically the millions who served in WWII, Korea, Vietnam, Iraq, Afghanistan, and countless other operations.

Current chaos and cuts to the Veterans Administration have already hobbled the system. Internal VA emails reveal that thousands of the 9 million veterans currently receiving benefits are already enduring gut wrenching cuts. These include loss of cancer treatments, loss of temporary housing for homeless vets, and loss of PACT Act protections to vets exposed to burn pits and other atrocities. Proposed downsizing of VA staff by 70,000 and DOGE-proposed closures of more than17 hospitals will be catastrophic.

Come join us Friday June 6th from 11:30-1:30 at the Burnsville NC Square to support veterans, the US Constitution, and the Declaration of Independence. The event will include readings of both documents, and will include “take-the-oath” ceremonies for any citizen wanting to take the oath to protect and defend the constitution. Anyone who has already taken the oath as part of their job requirement, such as civil servants, politicians, lawyers, judges, or anyone else, may come to re-commit to their oath by re-taking it.

“All US residents, including our bravest —our veterans — are entitled to the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” said Lea Charlton, a co-founder of Mountain Indivisible of WNC. “We should all be committed every day to protecting those rights.” Mountain Indivisible of WNC is sponsoring the event. It organizes pro-democracy events in Mitchell and Yancey Counties, and supports efforts in Avery County.

title: NO KINGS Little Rock
description:
NO KINGS (or Oligarchs or Kleptocrats) Flag Day MARCH for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

Join us on Saturday, June 14th at 10:00 AM for the Flag Day March for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion—a bold, peaceful demonstration across the Broadway Bridge in Little Rock, Arkansas. We march to uplift the voices of the marginalized, to call for justice in our communities, and to affirm that diversity, equity, and inclusion are not optional—they are essential.

📍Meet-up spot: Margaret Clark Adventure Park (Little Rock Riverfront Park) under the Broadway Bridge

🅿️ PARKING INFORMATION:

UNDER THE BROADWAY BRIDGE- This parking location is right next to the meet-up spot and is accessible to those who have mobility needs. 

If you start in front of the Robinson Center, you will go WEST on Markham Street, cross over Broadway Street, and take the first right on Bruce Moore/Arch Street. This street dead-ends at the parking lot.

OTHER PARKING: You are also welcome to park anywhere downtown. If you park downtown near Robinson Center/The Old State House Museum/Doubletree Hotel—
Walk down Conway Street (which runs between Doubletree Hotel and Old State House Museum), over the pedestrian bridge, and that will lead you directly to our meeting spot.

🗓️ SCHEDULE:

9:30AM- Begin gathering at the above Meet-Up spot (more details, maps, and flyers to follow)

10:00AM- Walk across the Broadway Bridge, turn around at NLR Riverfront Park, walk back across the bridge.

~10:45AM- Short Rally @ The Meet-Up Spot

The short rally at the end will include speakers, music, and a united call to action.

🧳 PLEASE BRING:

👟Comfortable shoes
💦 Water!!
☀️Weather-appropriate clothing
🧴Sunscreen
🪧Protest Signs, Flags, and Umbrellas

☂️PROTEST UMBRELLAS:

Decorate an umbrella with protest messages to use as shade!

June 14th also marks Donald Trump’s birthday, a day he has chosen to celebrate with talk of military parades and authoritarian posturing. We reject fear-mongering and exclusion. Instead, we choose unity. While others parade power, we march with purpose. We show the world that our strength lies in compassion, community, and collective action.

We believe that diversity strengthens us, equity uplifts us, and inclusion unites us. Whether you’re marching for racial justice, LGBTQ+ rights, accessibility, gender equity, immigrant protections, or education equity—your voice matters here.

Let’s reclaim June 14th as a day of people power. Together, we march—for a world where everyone belongs.

Volunteers

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America
description:
## **People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America**

The United States is not a corporation, and our government is not a for-profit enterprise. Elon Musk is not a government official. He’s a billionaire with no accountability to the American people, and nobody voted for him. Our democracy deserves better.

Musk and Trump will only be defeated by a massive, bipartisan movement of everyday Americans standing up against corruption, authoritarianism, and huge tax breaks for the rich, while fighting for the programs that working people need.

** This is a BIPARTISAN, PEACEFUL Protest** 
**No violence or Destruction of Property will be tolerated** 

**The People over Profit Movement**

Right now, millions of Americans across the political divide are struggling. 60% live paycheck to paycheck, many earn very low wages, and 85 million lack proper health insurance. College is too expensive for young people, a quarter of seniors live on $15,000 a year or less, and childhood poverty is among the highest in the world. We also face a severe shortage of affordable housing.

At the same time, the wealthiest Americans, like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg, are getting richer. Since Trump’s election, their combined wealth has grown by over $200 billion—more than the bottom half of the country. Meanwhile, the middle class shrinks, and democracy is at risk.

Our goal is to protect democracy and create an economy that works for everyone, not just the rich. As the wealthiest country in the world, we have the potential to use new technologies to improve everyone’s lives, but instead, most of the wealth goes to the people who need it the least.

We must make healthcare a human right, raise wages to a living standard, improve public education, address the housing crisis, create good-paying jobs to fight climate change, and end all forms of discrimination.

**We the People believe that in the richest country in the history of the world we must establish that:**

1. Healthcare is a human right and must be available to all regardless of income.

2. Every worker in America is entitled to earn a decent income. We must raise the minimum wage to a living wage and make it easier for workers to join unions.

3. We must have the best public educational system in the world, from childcare to vocational training, to graduate school – available to all.

4. We must address the housing crisis and build the millions of units of low-income and affordable housing that we desperately need.

5. We must create millions of good paying jobs as we lead the world in combating the existential threat of climate change.

6. We must abolish all forms of bigotry.

title: Join the National Day of Action for Single Payer Healthcare!
description:
## It’s time to end the health care crisis. Join the National Day of Action for Single Payer! 
**Saturday, May 31st 12pm-4pm**

Join us at 12pm to connect with our incredible sponsor organizations — get plugged in with groups leading transformative work in our communities. Then at 1pm, we’ll kick off a powerful program featuring speakers fighting to make universal healthcare a reality in our state.

Our health care system is broken—and it’s **killing** us. For-profit insurers and corporate middlemen deny care, drive up costs, and profit off our pain. Decades of piecemeal reforms have only made things worse: skyrocketing prices, massive waste, and some of the worst health outcomes among wealthy countries.

**We say: enough.**

### We demand a system that puts people before profit—where health care is treated as a human right, not a business.

#### We are calling for:

- The elimination of private insurance companies and for-profit care.

- A national, publicly funded single payer program that covers everyone—comprehensively and equitably.

- A transformation of our health care system to serve communities, not corporations—freeing caregivers from corporate control and putting power in the hands of the people.

This event is happening in Portland, but we’re not stopping here. Activists are organizing sister actions across Oregon—from the coast to the high desert. Stay tuned for more info on how to plug in near you!

On the **National Day of Action**, people across the country—patients, nurses, union members, small business owners, neighbors and organizers—will take to the streets to demand real change. This is about building a mass movement to take profit out of care and put National Single Payer on the political agenda—now.

Bring your families (kid friendly!), neighbors, friends, everyone you know and join us to turn collective outrage into collective action: put National Single Payer on the nation’s agenda!

For your mental and physical health, I recommend taking the occasional Saturday off! Know that others are there keeping the event going strong.

There may be individuals who approach on foot and try to provoke us.

It is a requirement of all attendees that you help uphold our commitment to non-violence and de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

Protests should not be aimed at attacking the business interests of Tesla or their customers.

• Stare past any agitators like they don’t exist. 
• Start a conversation about something random with someone near you.

For your safety and the safety of those around you, consider not engaging with anyone that tries to provoke you.

Resist. Dissent. Persist.

Join our Rush-Hour Resistance Rally outside the Chalmers Wylie VA Clinic to protest the cuts to the VA and support veterans!

This huge facility, serving veterans from a wide area, is on James Road just south of the Columbus Airport. Thousands of cars pass this location during rush hour every weekday afternoon, making this the perfect place to inform people about the crippling cuts that Trump, Musk and DOGE are making to our federal government.

Demonstration area: We will be demonstrating on public sidewalks on both sides of James Road, which are highly visible to commuters passing by.

UPDATED PARKING INFO: To eliminate any possibility of getting in the way of patients or staff at the clinic, we are asking everyone to avoid using the VA lot to the east of James Road. Instead, please park west of James Road. Look for Visitor Parking signs in the lot for Africentric High School, 3223 Allegheny Ave, Columbus, OH 43209. Or you can park on three side streets—Kellner, Lowell and Edgevale—off Ruhl Ave., which is the first stoplight intersection south of the VA clinic. If you’re car-pooling, you should be able to drop off passengers on Allegheny Ave. just west of James, on the way to the Africentric parking lot.

Consider a double-sided sign so that you can have one message for Issa and another for the motorists. 

HANDS OFF:
Our bodies
Our healthcare
Our public lands
Our education 
Our human rights

Rallies are a great way to meet other like-minded community members. They remind us that we aren’t alone and it feels good to be civically engaged. Action is the antidote to despair. We guarantee you will feel better about the state of affairs when you leave this event. 

Please note that there is a mental health services business in Issa’s office. Please allow a direct path the elevator for patients at all times. Refrain from banging on the glass doors as it has been reported to upset some of the patients. Please follow all posted rules and traffic laws when attending a rally. title: March for Integrity
description:
**PLEASE REGISTER VIA OUR WEBSITE AT [moneyoutofpolitics.org/join](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/join)**

The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan march in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Finding Kean Fridays
description:
NEW LOCATION - PLEASE READ
Join fellow NJ - 07 constituents for a weekly gathering as we work to #FindKean. Constituents are visiting his office every Friday. Let’s keep that momentum going.

Since Junior abruptly left his office in Bernardsville, we've tracked him down to his new digs at 100 Corporate Drive, Lebanon, NJ 08833.

We will continue to meet at 100 Corporate Drive, Lebanon, NJ every Friday. 

We will gather in the parking lot and small groups (2 per visit) can go into his office to meet with staff. We'll provide suggested talking points based on the votes and events of the past week. There is also an area near Rt. 22 where we can rally, but please note that if you have mobility issues, you may want to skip the rally portion. Otherwise, the building is easily accessed by anyone, and there is plenty of parking.

For those who will rally, please note the following:
-- There is just a grassy hill between people and traffic. 
-- Prepare for the weather - rain gear, boots, tick spray, sunscreen
-- We don't anticipate trouble, but we don't yet know what police presence there may be, so remember that this is a peaceful rally and we should not engage if there are counter protesters.

Whether you speak from the heart or bring hard-hitting facts, you deserve a hearing from your elected official. But be respectful of the staff’s time, and that of your fellow constituents who are waiting. Many Fridayers find it helpful to focus on one or two current issues.

· If you are addressing a Congressman’s vote or challenging his position on the issues, a personal story makes a difference.
· Leave a letter at the end of your visit if you like; the staff must log and respond to all letters.
 A thank-you and a polite tone at all times are a must.

Come for five minutes or stay for an hour. The more of us who show up each Friday, the better.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:

**General Visibility Rules:**

* **Distance is Key:** The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
* **"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility:** A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
* **Bridge Specifics:** Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.

**Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:**

* **Go Big:** Aim for lettering that is at least **12-24 inches tall**, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
* **Bold, Simple Fonts:** Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
* **High Contrast Colors:** This is critical!
    * **Dark letters on a light background** (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
    * **Avoid low-contrast combinations** like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
    * **Limit your color palette** to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
* **Concise Messaging:** Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
* **Material and Construction:**
    * **Sturdy materials:** Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
    * **Weatherproof:** Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
    * **Double-sided signs:** If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
* **Test Your Signs:** Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
* **Spacing (Kerning):** Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.

By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
accessibility_notes:
Here are a couple of notes on logistics.
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers.  (Please note that if you become a customer, it’s fine to bring snacks to the rally that you have bought, but please take any empty snack containers back home with you, when you leave. In any case, no matter which direction you are coming from, if it is possible, please try to park before you reach the intersection to save on congestion and choose a spot as far away as you feel comfortable walking from, leaving closer spots to those who can’t walk as far.
The rally will start on the SE corner, but as more folks arrive, we will disperse to the SW, NW, and NE corners, as well.   If you cross from one side to another, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
 Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  
Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone,  who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked.
We will not have speakers. The plan will simply be to hold the signs we have made and wave, if that feels right.  We expect that a lot of passing cars will honk back in approval! 
Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards with badges reading  “Standing Rally Corner Captain or “Standing Rally Media/City Liaison”.  If you see other folks with “Press” marked on their clothing or who are giving direction to you, know that they are not part of Four Corners and are not endorsed or vetted by us.
See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersinLenexa to your post!
